findings.text: A gather context accepts folio page ranges for deferred invalidation and freeing, with a default single size form and a sized form that records whether reverse mapping work should be delayed.

Queued pages use one slot for a single page and two slots for a multi page range with the second slot holding the count, and the batch is advanced before fewer than two free slots remain so a future multi entry always fits.
The gather context keeps an embedded local batch plus a singly linked chain of heap batches with an active pointer, entry count, capacity and chain length, where the local batch serves as chain head.

Gather lifecycle moves from initialization with cleared range and raised pending count, through queuing and optional table batching, to a finish phase that flushes translations, releases tables and pages, frees overflow batches and drops the pending count.
A flush interface drains previously deferred reverse mapping removals for a given region by scanning the local batch and the active batch when distinct, then clears the deferred indicator.
When deferred reverse mapping work is pending, chaining beyond the local batch is disallowed, forcing an earlier flush rather than unbounded accumulation.
Empty table reclamation acquires the higher level table lock first and then the leaf lock with nesting when they differ, using a nonblocking attempt in the fast path and releasing in reverse order.
Table page reclamation is considered only when enabled at build time, explicitly requested for the current zap operation, and the range covers at least a full second level table span.

Clearing of nonpresent entries distinguishes device private and exclusive, genuine swap, migration, userfault markers, guard markers and poison markers, updating occupancy and references per class and preserving markers unless explicitly allowed to drop them.

Batch length for present entries is limited by caller maximum, remaining pages in the folio from the starting frame, and first mismatch of masked entry contents with expected successive frames, with optional folding of writability and age and dirtiness into the representative entry.

Swap batch length counts consecutive entries whose type is unchanged and whose offsets increase by one, retaining soft dirty and exclusivity and userfault indications when deriving the successor for comparison.

Cache interfaces report the next or previous missing offset within a bounded scan, treating absent slots and value coded shadow entries as misses and returning a past the end indicator when no miss appears in the window.
Cache entry lookup runs under read side protection, retries on invalidated traversals and on failed or stale reference acquisition, and returns value coded entries without raising a reference count.

Writeback completion clears reclaim desire with rotation to the reclaimable tail when appropriate, ends the writeback state with wakeup on last completion, accounts throttled writeback, and handles uncached invalidation in task context with an extra reference held across the sequence.

Fault time folio locking either returns a retry indication immediately or after releasing the fault lock and waiting, honoring killable waits and nowait requests, while non retryable faults block until ownership is obtained.

Asynchronous folio lock attempts enqueue the waiter and mark waiters present under the waitqueue irq lock before trying ownership, dequeuing promptly on success and reporting a queued status on contention.
Overflow batch creation can fail due to chain length cap or page allocation failure, in which case queuing reports that the caller must flush before continuing rather than losing the entry.
Encountering a nonpresent encoding outside the known device, swap, migration, marker and poison classes triggers an alert and a one time warning while still clearing the slot.

When nested batching is detected at finish time, the operation escalates to whole address space scope with reset range and marks tables as freed to avoid stale translations from concurrent batched updates or freed tables.

Table freeing has build dependent behavior, either invalidating walker caches and deferring reclamation through a grace period or freeing directly, with a no operation variant when table batching is disabled.

Per address space batched invalidation tracks pending versus flushed counts in one atomic word, flushing the whole space only when they differ and preserving newly arrived pending work via compare exchange.
A helper returns the leaf entry address for a given second level entry and address while also reporting which leaf lock protects it, without acquiring that lock.
Laundering succeeds trivially when the folio is clean or belongs elsewhere or the holder lacks a launder operation, otherwise it delegates to the holder routine and propagates its result.

Encoded page reclamation drains batches in bounded chunks, counting entries normally but counting underlying pages when poisoning or zeroing on free is active, yielding the processor between chunks and preserving multi entry pairs across chunk boundaries.
